Foundations: Points, Lines, and Planes: A location with no size or dimension
A straight path extending forever in both directions
A flat surface extending forever in all directions
Part of a line with two endpoints
Part of a line with one endpoint extending forever in one direction
Points lying on the same line
Points lying in the same plane
The point dividing a segment into two equal parts
A line, ray, or segment cutting another segment into two equal parts
A figure formed by two rays sharing an endpoint
An angle measuring less than 90 degrees
An angle measuring between 90 and 180 degrees
Logic and Proof: The if part of a conditional statement
The then part of a conditional statement
Swapping the hypothesis and conclusion of a conditional
Negating both the hypothesis and the conclusion
Swapping and negating both parts, always logically equivalent to the original
An if-and-only-if statement, true in both directions
A single case that disproves a general statement
Drawing a conclusion from accepted facts and rules
Forming a general conjecture from observed patterns
A statement accepted as true without proof
A statement proven true using postulates and logic
A proof listing statements beside their justifications
Parallel and Perpendicular Lines: Lines meeting at a right angle
A line crossing two or more other lines
Matching-position angles at each intersection, congruent when lines are parallel
Angles inside the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal
Angles outside the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal
Interior angles on the same side of the transversal, supplementary when lines are parallel
Opposite angles formed by intersecting lines, always congruent
Two adjacent angles forming a straight line, summing to 180 degrees
Lines that are not coplanar and never intersect
Congruent Triangles: Congruent figures
Figures with the same shape and the same size
SSS congruence
Three pairs of equal sides prove triangles congruent
SAS congruence
Two sides and the angle between them prove triangles congruent
ASA congruence
Two angles and the side between them prove triangles congruent
AAS congruence
Two angles and a non-included side prove triangles congruent
HL congruence
For right triangles, hypotenuse and one leg prove congruence
CPCTC
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent
Included angle
The angle formed between two named sides
Included side
The side lying between two named angles
Isosceles triangle
A triangle with at least two congruent sides
Equilateral triangle
A triangle with all three sides congruent
Scalene triangle
A triangle with no congruent sides
Relationships Within Triangles: Median of a triangle
A segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side
Altitude of a triangle
A perpendicular segment from a vertex to the opposite side
Angle bisector
A ray dividing an angle into two equal angles
Perpendicular bisector
A line cutting a segment in half at a right angle
Centroid
The point where the three medians meet, the balance point
Circumcenter
Where the perpendicular bisectors meet, equidistant from the vertices
Incenter
Where the angle bisectors meet, equidistant from the sides
Orthocenter
The point where the three altitudes meet
Midsegment
A segment joining two midpoints, parallel to and half the third side
Triangle inequality theorem
Any two sides must sum to more than the third side
Exterior angle theorem
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles
Triangle sum theorem
The interior angles of a triangle total 180 degrees
Similarity: Similar figures
Same shape, proportional sides, congruent angles
Scale factor
The ratio of corresponding lengths between similar figures
AA similarity
Two pairs of congruent angles prove triangles similar
SSS similarity
Three pairs of proportional sides prove triangles similar
SAS similarity
Two proportional sides and the included angle prove similarity
Proportion
An equation stating two ratios are equal
Geometric mean
For a and b, the value x where a/x equals x/b
Dilation
A transformation that resizes a figure by a scale factor
Side-splitter theorem
A line parallel to one side divides the other two proportionally
Ratio of areas
For similar figures, the square of the scale factor
Ratio of volumes
For similar solids, the cube of the scale factor
Right Triangles and Trigonometry: Pythagorean theorem
In a right triangle, a squared plus b squared equals c squared
Hypotenuse
The side opposite the right angle, always the longest
Leg
Either of the two sides forming the right angle
Pythagorean triple
Three whole numbers satisfying the Pythagorean theorem, such as 3-4-5
Sine
In a right triangle, opposite over hypotenuse
Cosine
In a right triangle, adjacent over hypotenuse
Tangent
In a right triangle, opposite over adjacent
SOH-CAH-TOA
Mnemonic for the sine, cosine, and tangent ratios
Inverse trigonometric function
Used to find an angle when you know a side ratio
Angle of elevation
The upward angle from horizontal to a line of sight
Angle of depression
The downward angle from horizontal to a line of sight
45-45-90 triangle
An isosceles right triangle with sides in ratio 1 to 1 to root 2
30-60-90 triangle
A right triangle with sides in ratio 1 to root 3 to 2
Quadrilaterals and Polygons: Polygon
A closed figure made of straight line segments
Regular polygon
A polygon with all sides and all angles congruent
Convex polygon
A polygon with no interior angle greater than 180 degrees
Concave polygon
A polygon with at least one interior angle greater than 180 degrees
Parallelogram
A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Rectangle
A parallelogram with four right angles
Rhombus
A parallelogram with four congruent sides
Square
A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus
Trapezoid
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
Kite
A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides
Interior angle sum
For an n-sided polygon, 180 times the quantity n minus 2
Exterior angle sum
The exterior angles of any convex polygon total 360 degrees
Circles: Circle
The set of all points equidistant from a center point
Radius
A segment from the center to any point on the circle
Diameter
A chord passing through the center, twice the radius
Chord
A segment joining two points on a circle
Tangent to a circle
A line touching the circle at exactly one point
Secant
A line intersecting a circle at two points
Arc
A portion of the circumference of a circle
Central angle
An angle with its vertex at the center of the circle
Inscribed angle
An angle with its vertex on the circle, half its intercepted arc
Sector
A pie-slice region bounded by two radii and an arc
Segment of a circle
The region between a chord and its arc
Circumference
The distance around a circle, 2 pi r
Concentric circles
Circles sharing the same center but different radii
Area and Perimeter: The total distance around a two-dimensional figure
The number of square units covering a two-dimensional figure
One half the base times the height
One half the height times the sum of the two parallel sides
One half the apothem times the perimeter
The perpendicular distance from the center of a regular polygon to a side
A fraction of the circumference matching the central angle
A fraction of the circle's area matching the central angle
A shape made by combining simpler shapes
Surface Area and Volume: Surface area
The total area of all outer faces of a solid
Volume
The amount of space a solid occupies, in cubic units
Prism
A solid with two congruent parallel bases and rectangular sides
Cylinder
A solid with two congruent circular bases
Pyramid
A solid with one base and triangular faces meeting at an apex
Cone
A solid with a circular base tapering to a single point
Sphere
The set of all points in space equidistant from a center
Volume of a prism
Area of the base times the height
Volume of a pyramid
One third the base area times the height
Volume of a sphere
Four thirds pi times the radius cubed
Lateral area
The surface area excluding the bases
Cross section
The two-dimensional shape revealed by slicing a solid
Net of a solid
A flat pattern that folds up into the solid
Transformations and Symmetry: Transformation
A change in the position, size, or orientation of a figure
Translation
A slide of every point the same distance and direction
Reflection
A flip of a figure across a line of symmetry
Rotation
A turn of a figure about a fixed point
Dilation of a figure
A resize about a center point by a scale factor
Rigid motion
A transformation preserving size and shape, also called an isometry
Pre-image
The original figure before a transformation
Image
The resulting figure after a transformation
Line symmetry
A figure can be folded along a line into matching halves
Rotational symmetry
A figure looks unchanged after a rotation of less than 360 degrees
Composition of transformations
Applying one transformation and then another
Glide reflection
A translation combined with a reflection
Coordinate Geometry: Distance formula
The Pythagorean theorem applied to coordinates to find segment length
Midpoint formula
Averaging the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates of two points
Slope formula
Change in y divided by change in x between two points
Proving a parallelogram
Show both pairs of opposite sides have equal slopes
Proving a rectangle
Show it is a parallelogram with perpendicular adjacent sides
Proving a rhombus
Show all four sides have equal length
Equation of a circle
(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 with center (h, k)
Partitioning a segment
Finding a point dividing a segment in a given ratio
Coordinate proof
Using coordinates and algebra to prove a geometric claim
Reflection over the x-axis
Negating the y-coordinate of every point
Probability in Geometry: Geometric probability
Probability found from a ratio of lengths, areas, or volumes
Sample space
The set of all possible outcomes
Independent events
Events where one occurring does not affect the other
Dependent events
Events where one occurring changes the probability of the other
Mutually exclusive events
Events that cannot both happen at once
Complement of an event
All outcomes where the event does not happen
Conditional probability
The probability of an event given that another has occurred
Permutation
An arrangement of items where order matters
Combination
A selection of items where order does not matter
Expected value
The long-run average outcome, weighted by probability
